content.title: Big Ten wrestling championships Day 2 results, NCAA qualifiers: Penn State wins
content.text: Updated March 8, 2026, 8:15 p.m. ETThe No. 1 team in NCAA wrestling flexed its muscles at Day 1 of the 2026 Big Ten wrestling tournament Saturday, March 7.In front of a home crowd at the Bryce Jordan Center, Penn State placed eight wrestlers in finals matches for Day 2 of the tournament while taking a commanding lead in the team standings, where it entered the day with 146.5 points. That lead helped the Nittany Lions to win the Big Ten championship title.The Nittany Lions finished with 184 points over the two-day event, with Ohio State and Nebraska rounding out the top three with 148.5 and 116.5 points respectively.Stream Big Ten wrestling tournament with Fubo (free trial)Cael Sanderson's squad looked well on its way to claiming a fourth straight Big Ten title, matching a program record. Of the eight Nittany Lions that sent in finals matches on Sunday, seven of them won their matches, including a TF by Josh Barr over Camden McDaniel in the 197-pound match.The Big Ten Conference also filled out its remaining allocations for the 2026 NCAA wrestling tournament, with the conference claiming a nation-leading 87 allotments, 24 more than the Big 12 in second place (63).USA TODAY Sports provided live updates to the team standings, brackets and NCAA qualifiers from Day 2 of the Big Ten wrestling championship: Big Ten wrestling championships standingsLast updated at 7:30 p.m. ET. Session IV will air on the Big Ten Network. Streaming options for that session also include Fubo, which offers a free trial to potential subscribers.Big Ten wrestling championships start time todayDate: Sunday, March 8Time: Noon ET (Session III) | 4:30 p.m. ET (Session IV)Location: Bryce Jordan Center (University Park, Pennsylvania)Day 2 of the Big Ten wrestling tournament will begin at noon ET (11 a.m. CT) from the Bryce Jordan Center in University Park on March 8. Session III will comprise consolation semifinals and seventh-place matches, while Session IV (beginning 4:30 p.m. ET) will comprise first-, third- and fifth-place matches.
